Verdict

No confirmed signs of a malicious supply-chain compromise. Overall risk: **info**.

Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators.

Automatic Execution Paths

  • pyproject.toml uses the hatchling.build backend. In the provided content, there is no evidence of install-time arbitrary execution via setup.py, .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, or malicious custom PEP 517 hooks.
  • [project.scripts] jarify = "jarify.cli:main" is a normal console_scripts entry point and requires user invocation. It is not evidence of malicious automatic execution.
  • src/jarify/__init__.py only contains a version string and shows no malicious import-time side effects.
  • File reading/writing, stdin handling, and config discovery in src/jarify/cli.py appear consistent with a SQL formatter/linter CLI and do not indicate install-time or interpreter-startup execution.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Obfuscation

  • The provided files show no evidence of broad credential discovery, .env/SSH/cloud/kube/CI token harvesting, archive staging, external upload, webhook/C2 exfiltration, persistence registration, Kubernetes/cloud metadata access, or Docker socket access.
  • .github/workflows/* uses Doppler secret fetching, GitHub App token generation, and PyPI OIDC publishing, but these appear to be normal release automation. No token theft or workflow-injection behavior was identified.
  • files.pythonhosted.org URLs and hashes in uv.lock appear to be normal dependency lockfile metadata, not attacker-controlled exfiltration endpoints or staging evidence.
  • Regex and placeholder-masking logic in parser.py appears to support SQL/Rust format placeholder parsing. There is no evidence of eval/exec, base64/zlib/marshal loaders, or obfuscated staged payloads.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • Within the provided file set, there is no evidence of hidden payloads, unexplained native binaries, typosquatting, suspicious dependency insertion, or wheel/sdist mismatch.
  • .github/workflows, .mise/tasks, and .agents documentation are present in the sdist, but the provided contents appear to be development/release automation and agent guidance files. There is insufficient evidence to treat them as malicious distribution-integrity anomalies.

Additional Verification Needed

  • Only selected text files from 165 extracted files were provided, so the full file list and unprovided file contents were not reviewed.
  • No wheel artifact was provided, so sdist-vs-wheel mismatch could not be assessed.
  • The presence or absence of large/binary files cannot be fully confirmed from the provided excerpts alone.
